laws.rule: South Australia says flying a drone over its national parks, conservation parks, game reserves, recreation parks, regional reserves or marine park restricted-access zones without a permit is an offence. The authority considers permits for scientific research and commercial filming only.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: South Australia National Parks says amateur filming and photography in its national parks do not require a permit, while commercial filming and photography do. Drone use is a separate permission.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: Most South Australian national parks do not allow dogs or other pets; some allow pets on leads in specified places. Check the park page before taking an animal.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: South Australia parks guidance says collecting firewood from a park is prohibited. Check whether fires are allowed at the specific park, as well as current fire bans and closures; the agency says all its parks close on catastrophic fire danger days.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Aboriginal first nations implore visitors to respect their traditional lands and waters. In the absence of site-specific protocols, National Parks and Wildlife Service SA encourages visitors to show respect by not touching or removing anything from a cultural site, to respect the wishes of Traditional Owners when access is restricted, and to take all rubbish when they leave.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: A number of Aboriginal cultural sites are promoted on the parks website, but some sites are not open to visitors. Sites of significance according to Aboriginal tradition, and sites significant to Aboriginal archaeology, anthropology and history, are protected by the Aboriginal Heritage Act 1988. Read the Traditional Owners section on the individual park page to learn whose Country you are visiting.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: National Parks and Wildlife Service South Australia, with co-management boards and Aboriginal partners.
culture-and-protocol.note: Statewide parks visitor guidance only. Site-specific protocols, where published on a park page, take precedence.
